data.name: Yiskah
data.gender_notes: Yiskah is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Yiskah means 'God hears'. This name is associated with the Hebrew prophetess Hagar, who is remembered for her faith and her relationship with God. In the Old Testament, Hagar is the Egyptian slave girl who becomes the mother of Ishmael, the ancestor of the Arab people. The name Yiskah carries the meaning “God hears” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew. Parents who choose Yiskah usually hope their child will grow to embody god hears and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that represents faith and trust in God.
data.etymology: Yiskah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God hears.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Yiskah total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Yiskah carries a rich cultural heritage, linking it to the ancient Hebrew tradition and the Judeo-Christian religious history. It is a name that is deeply rooted in the religious and cultural context of the Middle East. The name Yiskah is more commonly used in its English variant, 'Isabella' or 'Isabel', which has become a popular name in Western cultures as well.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, the name Yiskah carries a powerful meaning, reminding us of our connection to God. It is a name that instills hope and faith, encouraging us to trust in God's hearing and answering of our prayers. The name Yiskah is also a reminder of the biblical prophetess Hagar, who, despite her difficult circumstances, remained steadfast in her faith and trusted in God's loving care for her and her son, Ishmael. In this way, the name Yiskah embodies the spirit of strength, faith, and perseverance, inspiring those who bear this name to emulate the characteristics of Hagar and to seek the wisdom and guidance of God in their lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Yiskah, meaning "God is my source of laughter," reflects the joy and lightness of faith in God, reminding us to find happiness and joy even in the most trying times. It is a reminder to seek God in the simple pleasures of life and to find His presence in moments of merriment and celebration.

biblical_reference.note: The name Yiskah is not found in the Bible, but its roots in Hebrew are associated with devotion and worship.

historical_references.reference: In the Old Testament, Yiskah (also known as Tamar) is the daughter of Eljah and the wife of Judah. She disguises herself and deceives Judah, resulting in the birth of twins Zerah and Pharez. This event takes place before King David's reign in the late 11th century BCE.

In the New Testament, Yiskah (also known as Rachel) is mentioned as a disciple of Jesus. She is believed to have been the wife of the apostle Cleopas and is often identified with the unnamed 'woman of Sychar' in the Gospel of John. This occurs during the ministry of Jesus, around 27-30 CE.

In modern usage, Yiskah is often used as a symbol of wisdom, insight, and creativity.
